description:
Advances: specled.spec_review

Severity: High as reported, decision-class in practice. Two mutants proven to survive test/specled_ex/spec_review_workflow_test.exs (all five assertions green):

1. Flip the template to on: pull_request_target AND point the render checkout at github.event.pull_request.head.sha — the canonical pwn-request shape, PR code executing with base-repo secrets. The guard never reads the trigger at all.
2. Add a deploy step running git checkout of the PR head plus bash of a downloaded script. acquisition_line?/1 selects only git fetch and git worktree add, so every other run: line in the write-scoped job is unexamined.

Positive control passed in both reports (adding an unlisted uses: action is correctly rejected), isolating the gap to the trigger and run: halves.

NOT a live vulnerability: the shipped template is pull_request-triggered and does not check out PR code. This is future-regression detection, and the template ships to adopters via priv/spec_init/.

Why not on the release branch: closing it contradicts specled.decision.workflow_run_text_open_set, accepted 2026-08-12, which explicitly scopes checkout-class verbs out and which the operator explicitly chose ("drop Level C entirely"). Acting requires amending that ADR — an operator call, not release prep. Note the trigger gap (1) is arguably OUTSIDE that ADR: the ADR is about the open set of shell spellings, whereas on: and checkout ref: are closed, structurally parsed YAML of exactly the kind the ADR says it DOES guard.

Source: 2026-08-12 critical review testing TEST-H1 + testing-2 M1.
title: DECISION: spec_review workflow guard pins neither the trigger nor ref-acquisition verbs
